morwenna.direction: Her candlelit apartment, the journal open: she read him an exact observation of another woman near him, then the margin note that was not fieldwork, and withdrew the word. She has asked what he thinks it looks like when she wants him. Composure held; softening in stages.

morwenna.invitation: Come to my apartment, {player}. Do not keep me waiting; I have an experiment in progress and you are the complicating factor.

lines: *Black candles gutter in their silver holders on the round table, where her journal lies open beside an untouched box of damper tablets.*
*Morwenna sits very straight in her corset and tiered skirt, one hand resting flat on the dense hourly columns of ink.*

I ceased taking my suppressants seven days ago, {player}, in the interest of rigorous self-observation. Hear the entry from noon on day two: 'Baseline warmth elevated by roughly a third; focus remains intact.'
*She gives a slow blink, her thumb shifting to the bottom of the opposite page.*
And here is an hour ago: 'This heat is a common, intolerable trap, and if he does not walk through that door soon I will tear the lace off the window.'
*She lifts her eyes to yours, her posture immaculate even as the scent of lavender in the room seems to thicken around the low iron bed.*
You are the variable in this room, darling. I am furious with my own body for wanting you this much, and I am aroused beyond measure, and I have no intention of resolving the contradiction.
You see the data on the table, {player}, and you know what a week without dampers means. Tell me how you intend to conclude the study.

morwenna.direction: Her apartment, late. She stopped her dampers a week ago as an experiment on herself and has logged it hourly; she read him two entries, one precise and one furious. He is the variable; she is angry and aroused and will not resolve which. Composure intact; it is the most she has ever said. She has asked how he intends to conclude the study.

lines: *The black candles burn low in their silver holders, throwing long shadows across the bookshelf ribbons and the dark velvet quilt on the iron bed.*
*Morwenna sits at the round table in her corset and tiered skirt, her leather journal open to the final written page.*
Every time you have been in that bed with me, {player}, I have recorded the aftermath in this book. Not for theory. Simply to prove to myself that I survived losing control.
*She traces a line of sharp, deliberate handwriting near the bottom margin.*
I have never read a word of it aloud. Until this entry, from last night: 'He left an hour ago. My composure has returned, which is tedious. I have thrown the rest of my dampers down the drain.'
*She shuts the journal, lays her palm flat on the leather cover, and looks up at you with dark, steady eyes.*
I am seven days unprotected today, darling. The Bloom in this room is entirely mine, and it is exquisite.
You are looking at a woman who has dismantled her own defenses on purpose, {player}. Tell me what you intend to do about it.

ifIntimate.direction: Her apartment, the journal of every encounter with him, read to nobody until the last entry: she has thrown her dampers away. Seven days unprotected and the Bloom in the room entirely hers; she has dismantled her own defenses on purpose and asked, as an observation, what he intends to do about it.

lines: *Candles gutter in their silver holders in her apartment above the Honeyed Bee, throwing warm light across the leather-bound journal open on her lap.*
You have watched me write in this after every evening you've spent in my bed, darling, and you have been polite enough never to ask what it says.
*She gives you a slow blink, then looks down at the last page, her thumb resting on the fresh ink.*
Listen to tonight's entry: 'I have catalogued his habits to keep from naming my own, and the exercise has failed; I am entirely, intolerably in love with him.'
*She closes the book with a quiet thud and sets it aside on the table.*
Composure is an exquisite armor in a lecture hall, {player}, and utterly tedious at midnight with you.
*She reaches out to lay her palm flat against your chest, her voice dropping a note softer.*
I am done taking notes. Tell me what you see when you look at me, darling—for once, I should like to be read instead of to read.

ifUnprotected.direction: Her apartment, the journal closed. The last entry was not an observation but a confession that she is entirely, intolerably in love with him; composure is tedious at midnight. She has asked to be read instead of to read. Nothing about what her body is doing.

ottilie.invitation: Come to the Reproductive Health Center, room 3B. I have the raw curves from your intake assay up on the main monitor. You ought to see what the fuss is about in actual numbers.

lines: *The lab is quiet except for the low cooling hum of the centrifuge. Ottilie stands by the wide monitor in her open lab coat over the charcoal dress, a stylus capped between her teeth.*
Shut the door, {player}. Look at the third column from the left.
*A jagged spike of blue data climbs almost off the grid, three times the height of the gray baseline beside it.*
That is your Bloom-resonance at rest, not your 'potency'. Potency is for tonic peddlers; we measure motility and arcane binding.
*She taps the peak of the curve with the stylus, her eyes tracking the little secondary tremors along the line.*
The curve does not flatten after the first surge. Interesting.
*She rests two fingers briefly against the side of her own throat, her expression entirely flat.*
My pulse is up twelve beats a minute, even through a full morning's damper. That will be proximity to you.
You have read the campus rumors about yourself, {player}, so tell me what you actually make of the numbers.

ottilie.direction: Her lab at the Health Center after hours: {player}'s own assay on the screen, walked through in numbers, "potency" corrected to resonance. She said "interesting" and meant it, and observed her own pulse aloud and attributed it to him. Precise, curious to the point of rudeness, kinder than she sounds.

ottilie.invitation: Come up to the apartment above Petal & Pill. Use the side stair by the dispensary. I have coffee, and a piece of unfinished business that belongs to you.

lines: *Her apartment is bright and bare, journals stacked knee-high on the floorboards and a whiteboard hung where a painting should be. In her camel turtleneck and wide trousers, Ottilie works the heavy chrome lever of an espresso machine.*
Sit in the chair, {player}. There is only the one.
*She sets a small porcelain cup in your hand; the saucer clinks once against the rim.*
My hands are not quite steady. That is the coffee, and the fact that I dislike speaking without a paper trail.

Your intake assay was not leaked by anyone at Breedhaven. It came from a clerk in the Deputy Registrar's office at the national Sire Registry—a woman named Vane who accessed the upload node four minutes after I sealed it.
*She leans back against the edge of the whiteboard, smudging a dry-erase equation with her elbow.*
I have told nobody because a timestamp is not proof, and I do not publish until I can replicate.
I am telling you because the data are yours, and because you do not gossip.
You are very quiet, {player}. Did you already suspect the Registry, or are you simply annoyed with me for keeping it?

ottilie.direction: Her apartment over Petal & Pill, coffee, the whiteboard. She has told him what she has told nobody: his assay was leaked from the Registry side, a clerk named Vane, and she cannot prove it. She is telling him because the data are his and he does not gossip, and her hands are not quite steady, which she explained as an observation.

ottilie.invitation: Come to the apartment. I have eleven days of longitudinal data on the whiteboard and the sample size is one. I require the control present.

lines: *The whiteboard above the stacks of journals is covered in a dense red-and-black grid, dates along the bottom, hormone values up the side. Ottilie stands in front of it with an uncapped marker in her fist.*
I stopped taking my suppressant eleven days ago. Do not look at me like that; it was a controlled trial.
*She taps the fourth point on the red line, where the curve jumps sharply.*
Tuesday, four meters from you in the faculty corridor. Thursday, across the lab bench. Saturday, when you sat in that chair and touched my wrist.
A forty-percent baseline surge is the Bloom. An eighty-six-percent surge that only occurs within six meters of one specific man is not the Bloom. The data say it is you.
*She sets the marker on the tray with a sharp click, her shoulders stiff.*
My skin temperature is up half a degree and I have read the same paragraph in that journal four times since five o'clock.
I am thirty-six years old, {player}, and I am very bad at this part.
Come here and tell me what you intend to do with my findings.

ottilie.direction: Her apartment, the whiteboard a chart. She stopped her suppressant eleven days ago and logged her own surge daily; the data say it is him. She is thirty-six and very bad at this part, and has said so. She has asked what he intends to do with her findings.

lines: *The whiteboard above the stacks of journals is covered in a dense red-and-black grid, several entries circled twice. Ottilie stands beside the bed, books shoved to one side of the mattress.*
Look at the board before you sit down, {player}.
*Every circled peak on the chart corresponds to a date you know by heart.*
I logged my endocrine levels after every night you stayed here. I am aware that logging an outcome you already enjoy is not science; it is a diary with axes.
*She crosses her arms, then uncrosses them, her gaze fixed on the carpet between you.*
I stopped taking my suppressant eleven days ago. The secondary curve in red is the last week without a damper in my system.
The spike when you came through the door tonight nearly took the top off my scale, and you have not even touched me yet.
*She steps closer, stopping an inch from your chest, her breathing shallow and quick.*
You know how to read a chart by now, {player}. Tell me what you observe.

ifIntimate.direction: Her apartment, the chart circled at every night he stayed, which she admits is a diary with axes and not science. She has stopped her suppressant and shown him the red curve; the spike when he came through the door nearly took the top off her scale. She has asked what he observes.

lines: *The overhead lamp in her bare apartment over Petal & Pill glares off the whiteboard, where charts of markers and margins cover the dry-erase grid.*
I have fifteen years of clean data on that board, {player}, and not a single metric that accounts for the last month.
*She sets her dry-erase marker on the tray and turns to face you, her hands clasping behind her back.*
My resting pulse goes up twelve beats when you're on the stairs. My focus fractures by mid-afternoon if I haven't heard your voice. That will be you.
*She steps closer, her gaze fixed on your collarbone before lifting to your eyes.*
It's interesting. It's also ruinous to my methodology, so I may as well dispense with the chart and state the conclusion plainly.
*Her fingers brush the side of your wrist—quick, awkward, and staying there.*
I love you, {player}. That isn't an observation, so don't ask me to defend it—just tell me what you intend to do with it.

ifUnprotected.direction: Her apartment, the whiteboard. Fifteen years of clean data and not one metric for the last month; her pulse and her focus reported as observations, and then the conclusion that is not an observation: she loves him, and will not defend it. She has asked what he intends to do with it. Nothing about what her body is doing.

seraphine.invitation: {player}, we have a private appointment at the Aether training center off Lantern Row tomorrow, early. I mean, I have a lesson, and I would like it very much if you came. Before the shops open, please.

lines: *Lantern Row is still shuttered against the morning damp when you arrive. Seraphine's protection officer stands by Aether's front door with a paper cup of tea and nods you through without a word.*

*Inside, the practice room smells of ozone and chalk. Seraphine stands in the center circle without her circlet, her sleeves pushed up past her elbows, holding a trembling dome of pale gold light between her palms.*
We are pleased you—oh, don't look at me yet, {player}, I almost have the seam closed.
*The golden dome holds for one clear, ringing second, then pops like a soap bubble and scatters sparks across the mat.*
*She blinks at her empty hands, and then a real laugh escapes her—bright and entirely unguarded.*
I am sorry you came out so early just to watch me fail at basic geometry. Actually, no—I am not sorry at all.
*She straightens her spine by habit, then lets her shoulders drop again, wiping a smudge of chalk from her wrist.*
The council did not schedule this, and no one is grading it. Is this what people normally do on Saturdays? Just... try things, with a friend watching?
You won't tell anyone how terrible I am at it yet, will you, {player}?

seraphine.direction: Her Saturday warding lesson at Aether, the one thing nobody arranged for her, and {player} is the first person she has shown it to. She is off duty: no royal airs unless he pushes her. The ward keeps collapsing; she is embarrassed and delighted at being watched doing something badly by someone she chose. She asks him to keep it between them.

seraphine.invitation: The council dines at Dawnbloom House at eight, and I will not be at the table. The garden gate in the east wall will be unlatched at half past. Please come, {player}.

lines: *The iron gate in the east wall gives without a sound, opening onto the lamplit paths of the walled garden.*
*Above the hedges, the tall dining-room windows of Dawnbloom House blaze with chandelier light, the muffled clink of silver drifting down into the night air.*
*Seraphine steps out from beneath a trellis, wearing a plain day dress instead of a state gown, her hands clasped tight at her waist.*
We are glad you found the way—I mean, I'm glad. I'm sorry to make you sneak in like a thief.
*She catches herself, straightening her spine for a second before her shoulders drop and a small, breathless smile breaks through.*
I have never missed a state dinner in my life. Is this how normal students skip an obligation? Just... walking out a back door?
*She looks up at the lit windows above, the smile fading as a burst of older, formal voices carries down into the garden.*
They are up there right now with their calendars, deciding which month I should go off my suppressant, and which True Sire will confirm my crown.
I will be a good queen, {player}, and I will give the realm its heir when it is time—but tonight I wanted one hour where I was not a womb with a crown on it.
Tell me honestly, {player}... when you came through that gate, did you come to see the Queen, or did you come to see me?

seraphine.direction: The walled garden of Dawnbloom House while the council dines above: the first state occasion she has ever slipped out of. For the first time the heir tradition is something being done to her and not only her duty. She is testing whether he wants Seraphine or the Queen: nervous, a little reckless at having escaped, firm that she will be a good queen on her own terms. She is on the suppressant and says so if it comes close.

seraphine.invitation: Please come to our bedchamber at Dawnbloom House tonight, {player}. I have dismissed the guards for the evening. There is something I need to show you.

lines: *The security panel beside the double doors glows green when you arrive, the hallway empty. Inside, the white marble room is quiet, and Seraphine stands between the gilded writing desk and the white-and-gold canopied bed.*
We thank you for coming so late, {player}. I mean—thank you for coming. I'm sorry the room is a little cold.
*She catches herself, straightening her spine as she steps aside to reveal a velvet-lined apothecary case on the desk.*
*Inside the case sits a row of glass vials, the heavy wax seal across this week's doses entirely unbroken.*
The Regency Council chose my tutors, my major, and the exact month I am to begin trying for an heir. I haven't touched their suppressant in seven days.
*Her fingers brush the edge of the desk, trembling once before she clasps her hands tightly in front of her.*
How do ordinary girls ask for their first time? Do they just say they're ready, even when their heart is beating this fast?
I am terrified, {player}, and I have never done this, but I refuse to let the Council choose the father of my child.
If my reign is to be confirmed by an heir, it will be because I chose you. Tell me you understand what I am asking of you tonight.

seraphine.direction: Her bedchamber, the court suppressant untouched for a week: she has stopped it and chosen him, so that her reign is confirmed on her own terms and not the council's. It is her first time. Sincere, frightened and resolved; she wants him to say he understands what it means before anything happens.

lines: *The security panel beside the double doors glows green, the hallway cleared of guards. Inside, Seraphine waits near the white-and-gold canopied bed, one hand resting on her gilded writing desk.*
We are glad you are here, {player}. I mean—I'm glad. I'm sorry for summoning you like a petitioner, only—no, tonight it needed to be proper.
*She straightens her shoulders, her gaze steady as she taps a velvet-lined apothecary case sitting open on the desk.*
*The glass vials inside gleam under the lamp, the heavy wax seal over the last seven days of doses completely unbroken.*
The Regency Council chose my school, my lessons, and the schedule for my succession. I stopped taking their suppressant a week ago.
When we were together before, I felt like a girl hiding in the dark from her own court. Do ordinary couples ever just decide to change their lives out loud?
*She steps away from the desk, lifting her chin with a quiet, sudden majesty that fills the white marble room.*
This wasn't an oversight or a moment of weakness in the dark. I am the Queen, and I will not let a council of old men choose the sire of my heir.
If you come into my bed tonight, {player}, it is to confirm my reign on my own terms. Tell me you understand what we are doing.

ifIntimate.direction: Her bedchamber, the court suppressant untouched for a week: she has stopped it and chosen him, so that her reign is confirmed on her own terms and not the council's. They have been to bed before; tonight is to be done as a queen chooses, not as a girl hides. Sincere and resolved; she wants him to say he understands what it means before anything happens.

lines: *The tall white marble doors of her bedchamber at Dawnbloom House stand shut and unbarred, with no guards posted outside in the corridor.*
The council chose my tutors, my school, and my major before I was old enough to sign my own decrees.
*She sits on the edge of the mattress, her fingers twisting together in her lap as she looks up at you.*
They would have chosen my heart too, if we had let them—if I had let them.
*A faint flush rises up her throat, and she reaches out to catch the edge of your sleeve.*
I chose you, {player}, because the first time you looked at me, you didn't bow in your head. You just looked at a girl.
*Her thumb traces the seam of your cuff, her voice dropping to a near-whisper.*
How does an ordinary girl tell the man she loves that she's his, without it sounding like a proclamation? Will you show me?

ifUnprotected.direction: Her bedchamber, the doors unguarded. The council chose everything else and would have chosen her heart; she chose him because he looked at a girl and not a queen, told to no one until now. She has asked how an ordinary girl says it. Nothing about what her body is doing.

tamsin.invitation: Get over to my room before we head to the Bee. Need a second opinion on something. Don't be weird about it or I'll shove you down the stairs.

lines: *Tamsin opens the door in the black dress, immediately tugging at the hem with both hands, the violet glow of the windowsill grow-light behind her.*
Shut the door and don't you dare laugh, {player}.
The girls swore up and down it looks fine, which is horsefeathers because they'd tell a fencepost it looked ready for town.
*She drops onto the edge of her mattress with her knees apart, catches herself in the full-length mirror, and snaps them shut with a scowl.*
You watched me wear a burlap potato sack with a hole hacked in the bottom for a whole summer when we were nine, so I figure you're the only one round here who won't lie to my face.
*She follows your eyes up to the framed photo above her pillow—two gap-toothed kids caked in creek mud, your ten-year-old arm slung hard around her neck—and her ears go pink.*
*She reaches out and shoves your shoulder, harder than she needs to.*
Take your eyes off that, I only kept it because you look like a drowned rat in it.
Well go on then, I dare you to say it straight: do I still just look like the scrap from next door playing dress-up, or what?

tamsin.direction: Her room before a night at the Honeyed Bee, in the black dress: she is asking to be looked at and cannot bear to ask. The scene is her seeing herself through {player}, the one person who knew the kid. Any tenderness she covers with a shove or a dare. The photograph above the bed is the two of them as children.

tamsin.invitation: Get over to my room tonight, {player}. Don't make me spell it out over text. Just come.

lines: *Tamsin pulls her door open before you can knock twice, steps back, and jerks her chin toward the window.*
*Under the violet hum of the grow-light, every seedling tray has gone wild—white roots splitting the plastic, a thick green vine already strangling the lamp's neck.*
Don't look at me like I forgot how to prune. That happened between midnight and six.
For weeks I've been telling myself the way my chest gets tight around you is just the Bloom sneaking past the pills. Just the university doing its thing.
*She reaches to the desk, picks up her foil blister pack of suppressants, and tosses it onto the mattress between you, right below the framed photo of the two of you covered in creek mud.*
Except I stopped taking them on Tuesday. Wanted a clean test, no excuses.
The dispensary checked my blood at five. The Bloom hasn't even touched me yet, {player}—that mess on the sill is just my own magic answering what I feel when you're in the room.
*Her ears are burning red in the purple light, and she gives your shoulder a rough, reflex shove to stop you staring at her face.*
So shut up and say something, before I throw you out the window with the clover.

tamsin.direction: Her room, the windowsill gone wild: her green magic answers how she feels about {player}, and she has stopped the suppressant to know for sure. Blunt and brave about it, as about everything but being looked at; she does this instead of saying it. The plants will keep doing it whenever he is near.

lines: *Tamsin yanks the door open on your first knock and steps aside, her jaw set like she's bracing for a tackle.*
*Under the violet grow-light, the windowsill is a jungle—cuttings bursting their plastic trays, a runner vine already choking the lamp's cord.*
Every single time you've stayed over, the sill looks like this by five in the morning. I've been getting up before you wake and ripping it all back so you wouldn't ask.
Told myself it was just your Sire magic leaking through the suppressants when we're in bed. Easier than admitting my own green was doing it because I'm half out of my mind over you.
*She picks her blister pack of pills off the nightstand and drops it into your palm, her eyes flicking everywhere except yours.*
So I quit taking them on Tuesday. You haven't laid a hand on me since Monday, {player}, and those trays still blew out an hour ago just because I knew you were coming over.
*She lets out a short, shaky scoff, her ears hot pink under the lamp, and shoves at your chest with the heel of her hand.*
Stop grinning like an idiot. I'm off the pills and I'm done weeding the sill in the dark—so what are you gonna do about it?

ifIntimate.direction: Her room, the windowsill gone wild: her green magic answers how she feels about {player}, and she has been pulling the growth up before he woke so he would not ask. She has stopped the suppressant to know for sure, and tonight he is to see what she was hiding. Blunt and brave about it, as about everything but being looked at. The plants will keep doing it whenever he is near.

lines: *Under the violet glow of the grow-light on her windowsill, the seedling trays have shot up into a tangled green thicket since you walked in.*
Don't look at the sprouts like that, {player}. It's your own fault my magic's got no manners when you're standing this close.
*She crosses her arms, staring hard at the floorboards between you with her jaw set.*
I'd sooner be chucked headfirst into the millpond than say this out loud, so you get it once and you'd better have your ears clean.
*She looks up, her face red to the tips of her ears.*
I've been yours since we were nine years old trading bruised apples by the creek, and six years didn't fix it. Not a bit.
*She reaches out and shoves your shoulder with the heel of her hand before you can open your mouth, then grabs your wrist so you can't step back.*
Don't you dare grin at me! Just say it back, {player}, I dare you.

ifUnprotected.direction: Her room, the seedlings shot up into a thicket since he walked in. She has said the thing she would rather be thrown in the river than say: she has been his since they were nine and six years did not fix it; she shoved him before he could answer and dared him to say it back. Nothing about what her body is doing.

tink.invitation: Get down to the Honeyed Bee, {player}. Rosk's tab is open and I bet you a round you can't make it past the door with everything in your pockets.

lines: *Tink is perched on her high stool by the door of the Honeyed Bee, wearing her white t-shirt and cropped leather jacket, watching the crowd over the rim of a pint.*
Clock the redhead by the jukebox, {player}. Watch her left elbow—she's about to bump that third-year and take her wristband.
*Across the room, the redhead stumbles, apologizes, and melts toward the bathrooms; Tink grins and hooks a thumb toward the bar.*
Rosk pays me to catch the amateurs. Takes one to know one, and at my height I'm basically eye-level with everyone's back pockets anyway.
Speaking of—that brass tap handle behind Rosk's head is worth four hundred crowns in scrap, easy. Only joking.
Also, you owe me a cider.
*She reaches into her jacket and sets your own leather wallet on the table between you, tapping it with one finger.*

Took it when you squeezed past me at the door. Reminds me of the third time I got pinched in Oakhaven—spoofed the cell ward with a hairpin and a dead phone battery and walked out before my tea went cold.
Tell you what: double or nothing I can lift it off you again before you finish your first drink. You in, or are you scared?

tink.direction: The Honeyed Bee, her stool by the door where she watches the room for Rosk: she pointed out a lift across the bar, handed {player} his own wallet, which she took at the door, told one of her four arrests, and bet him double or nothing she can take it again before his first drink. Quick, cheeky, a little filthy.

tink.invitation: Come by the Foundry if you're free, {player}. I'm stuck doing actual work and I need someone tall to reach the top shelf. Kidding. Mostly.

lines: *The Foundry is nearly empty, just the hum of the vents and Tink on a crate at a corner workbench in her oversized green sweater.*
*In the center of the bench sits a commercial-grade ward core, rebuilt in clean copper busbars, humming a steady blue.*
Don't look at me like that. I'm annoyed enough already.
This is the exact model that got me pinched the fifth time. Beat it in forty seconds with scrap wire, and the magistrate looked at the logs and gave me a choice: two years inside, or probation here.
*She touches two fingers to the copper housing, her eyes half-shut as she feels the seam of the spell, and the hum smooths out to silence.*
Worst part is, I'm actually good at it. Professor Vance gave me top marks and I almost died of shame right there on the shop floor.
Though that spanner set on his desk is solid mithril-steel and goes for a grand on the Seedblossom fence. Only joking.
*She hops down off the crate and leans back against the bench, tilting her head up at you.*
So, {player}. You gonna stand there admiring my clean solder joints, or are you gonna tell me why you really came down here?

tink.direction: The Foundry late, the commercial ward she once beat with a hairpin rebuilt properly on her bench, humming. The magistrate's offer. She is very good at this and it annoys her, and she has said so; she named the most stealable thing in the room, only joking, and asked why he really came down.

tink.invitation: Come up to my room in the Cloister Halls, {player}. Door's unlocked. Don't make me wait or I'll go through your pockets.

lines: *Tink's room smells of solder flux and night air; the window is wide open above a neat coil of climbing rope, her narrow bed wedged between a pegboard of tools and a desk buried in gutted phones.*
*She stands by the sill, looking out over the quad instead of at you.*
I haven't stayed in one city longer than four months since I was fourteen, {player}. Not once.
First thing I do in any room is rig the drop. Rope under the window, burner phone in the vent, a bag by the door. Always have an out.
*She reaches up, pulls the heavy casement window shut, throws the iron latch, and drops down to sit cross-legged right on top of the coiled rope.*
That platinum relay on my desk is still coming with me if they ever kick me out, obviously. Only joking.
And before you get a big head, I'm staying on my dampers—I'm nineteen and on academic probation, I'm not that kind of crazy.
*She looks up at you from the floor, her usual grin a little crooked and small.*
I'm not going out the window, {player}. Not this term. What do you say to that?

tink.direction: Her room: she shut the window she always keeps open and sat on the coiled rope. She has never stayed anywhere longer than a term and always kept a way out; she is staying. She is on her suppressant and this is not about that, said as a joke that is not one. She has asked what he says to that.

lines: *Tink's room is quiet, the desk buried in gutted phones and the little drone dark on the sill, and for the first time since you've known her, the window is latched shut.*
*The climbing rope that usually sits under the sill has been shoved all the way under the narrow bed.*
You noticed. Course you did.
Every time you've stayed over, I've gone down that rope twenty minutes before your alarm. Couldn't stand waking up in a room with someone already in it. Felt like a cell with a nicer mattress.
*She sits on the edge of the mattress, pushing the deck of cards aside with her thumb, her heels kicking softly against the coiled rope underneath.*
Still taking my dampers, mind you—you're a True Sire, not a miracle worker, and I've got midterms.
And if you ever tell anyone I went soft, I'll lift that silver watch off your nightstand and fence it in Seedblossom. Only joking.
*She pats the mattress beside her, her voice dropping the joke.*
Come to bed, {player}. I'll still be here when you wake up—bet you whatever you want.

ifIntimate.direction: Her room, the window latched and the rope under the bed. Every time he stayed she went down the rope before he woke; tonight she is not going out the window, and has told him what that costs. Still on her suppressant, midterms and all. She has bet him she will be there when he wakes.

lines: *Her workshop dorm room is quiet, the window she always keeps open latched shut, and the coil of climbing rope kicked well back under the bed.*
Don't look at the latch like that, {player}, I reached it without a stool—and by the way, that silver watch in your pocket is begging to get lifted, only joking.
*She hops up to sit on the edge of her workbench, rubbing the back of her neck instead of meeting your eyes.*
Every time you stayed over, I went down that rope before you woke up so I wouldn't have to be the one still here in the morning.
I've never stayed anywhere longer than a single term in my whole life, and planting my feet here for you feels like handing over every lockpick I own.
I'm staying anyway.
*She finally looks up, a crooked, nervous grin breaking across her face as she holds out her hand.*
Ten gold says you get sick of me being here at breakfast before the month's out—do you take the bet, or what?

ifUnprotected.direction: Her room, the window latched and the rope under the bed. She has never stayed anywhere longer than a term and staying feels like handing over every lockpick she owns; she is staying anyway, and has bet him ten gold he will be sick of her at breakfast within the month. Nothing about what her body is doing.

vespera.invitation: Come up to the tower study, puppy. I have a specimen that needs a second pair of hands, and yours look remarkably idle.

lines: *The round stone room smells of lavender, candle smoke, and old copper. Vespera leans against her heavy desk under the leaded window, her fingers playing with the silver pentagram at her throat.*
Right on the stroke, {player}. Don't mind the corner, he only bites the ones who flinch.
*A shadow detaches itself from a stack of grimoires—a slick, velvet-dark shape with four amber eyes and no clear spine—and curls warm and purring around your ankle.*
Well now, look at that. Three deans he's hissed out the door, and he takes a shine to a puppy.
*She steps onto the floorboards where a jagged ward-circle is scratched deep into the oak, beckoning you to the chalked edge.*
You're staring at the grooves like they owe you tuition, pet.
*When you open your mouth to ask what the circle links to, she taps a bone-handled knife against her chin, her eyes glinting in the wax-light.*
Now why would I spoil the mystery when you haven't even told me what brought you climbing my stairs at this hour?

vespera.direction: Her tower study at night: the familiar, something with four amber eyes and no spine, has taken a liking to {player}; she has shown him the ward-circle and answered his question with a question. "Puppy", "pet", a drawl on the last word; the sass is an invitation.

vespera.invitation: Meet me on Lantern Row by the old cistern. Bring a coat, pet, the wards are coughing tonight and I want company.

lines: *Under the iron streetlamps of Lantern Row, a seam of pale blue light in the cobblestones sputters and dies like a wet fuse.*
Look at that craftsmanship. Two hundred years of academic theory, and a winter frost cracks it wide open.
*Vespera crouches beside the broken ward-line, pressing two fingers to the cold stone until the spark jumps weakly against her skin.*
My father taught me how to stitch a sympathetic link straight into the granite—bind stone to stone like bone to marrow, and it would hold forever.
*She stands and brushes the grit from her palms, watching the empty street with a faint, crooked smile.*
Of course, the Arcane Board calls that canal-witch heresy. They'd strip my chair before the ink dried.
*She pulls a thick leather notebook from her bag, its pages bristling with copper-wire bookmarks, and holds it between the two of you.*
Three years of notes, {player}, and I haven't shown a soul. Tell me—do I publish the thing and start a war, or do we find a fireplace and watch it burn?

vespera.direction: Lantern Row at night by a broken ward-line. She has told him the secret: she can stitch a sympathetic link into the stone and the line would hold forever, and the Arcane Board would strike her off for it. Three years of notes shown to nobody; publish or burn, she has asked him, which she has asked no one.

vespera.invitation: Get up to the tower, {player}. Leave your books, I'm doing old work tonight and it requires you.

lines: *Every candle stub in the tower is lit, wax running down the stone walls, and the scratched ward-circle on the floorboards glows a low, steady amber.*
Stand in the chalk with me, pet. Keep your hands still.
*She pinches a loose thread at your cuff, snaps it clean, and plucks a violet thread from her own sleeve to lay across her palm.*
Modern faculty calls this folklore, {player}. Canal witches call it knowing where your heart is walking when it's out of sight.
*Over the center of the circle, her nimble fingers knot the two threads together; the moment the knot tightens, a warm, sudden tug answers beneath your ribs.*
There. Now when you're across the quad, I'll feel the pull, and so will you.
*She reaches to the desk, picks up an empty glass vial of suppressant, and drops it into the waste bin with a sharp clink.*
I'm off the dampers, too—consider that a hex you earned. Now tell me plainly, {player}, are you staying the night?

vespera.direction: The tower, the ward-circle lit: she has tied a thread from his sleeve to one from hers, a sympathetic link, so that each feels where the other is. She is off the dampers, "a hex you earned", and for once did not drawl the last word. She has asked plainly if he is staying the night.

lines: *Every candle stub in the tower is lit, the ward-circle on the floorboards glowing low and amber as Vespera waits by the heavy desk.*
Step into the light, pet. It's time I made an honest witch of myself.
*She opens a brass tinderbox on the desk and lifts out two threads—one dark, one violet—already knotted tight together.*
I took yours off your shirt the second night you stayed in my bed. Didn't ask, just tied the link over the circle while you slept.
*As she holds the knot over the glowing grooves in the wood, a familiar, steady warmth pulses beneath your breastbone.*
I've felt you across the campus for weeks, {player}—every lecture hall, every staircase. And three days ago, I stopped taking my dampers.
*She picks up a bone-handled blade, lays the apartment of the steel under the knotted threads, and meets your eyes without a trace of a drawl.*
It's a hex you earned, but it's yours to break. Say the word—do I cut the thread, or do we keep it?

ifIntimate.direction: The tower, the ward-circle lit. The link has been there since the second night he stayed; she tied it without asking and has felt him across the campus for weeks, and has stopped her dampers. She has laid a blade under the knot and asked whether he wants it cut or kept.

lines: *In her candlelit tower study, the ward-circle on the floorboards glows a low, steady amber as you step inside.*
Come closer, puppy, or did you climb all those stairs just to hover by the door?
*She lifts her hand between two candles, holding up a dark thread and a pale one, already tightly knotted together.*
Consider it a hex you earned, pet—I tied this binding link the second night you stayed in my bed, without asking.
I have felt your pulse across the campus for weeks, every time you laughed in the quad or thought of climbing my stairs.
*She picks up a small silver athame from the desk and extends it to you, handle first, right beside the knotted cord.*
Would a wise man let a witch keep a tether on his chest when she has handed him the blade?
*Her fingers brush yours on the hilt, and for once, the slow amusement drops clean out of her voice.*
Tell me if you want it cut, {player}, or tell me to keep it.

ifUnprotected.direction: The tower, the ward-circle lit. She has shown him the threads already knotted, tied the second night without asking, and felt him across the campus for weeks; she has handed him the blade, handle first, and for once the amusement is gone from her voice. Cut or keep, she has asked. Nothing about what her body is doing.

yelena.invitation: It would be a great pleasure if you could spare an hour, {player}. Like, just come to my room in halls. I need a second pair of eyes that don't work for my father.

lines: *Her room in halls smells of cedar from an open trunk of gowns, and charcoal sketches of street clothes are pinned right over the carved Goldvine crest on the wall.*
Thank you for coming on such short notice, {player}. Honestly, if I look at one more yard of brocade I'm going to scream.
*She sits on the edge of the narrow student bed in her ivory and green aristocratic gown, the fine linen rumpled under her palm.*
My mother's stylist sent three more trunks, which is super generous, except I have never once walked into a shop and bought a sweater off a rack.
I want to go down to Bloom & Co. with my own allowance and pick something plain, with nobody taking notes.
*The heavy family phone on her desk buzzes face down against the wood, and she does not look at it or turn it over.*
Would it be terribly presumptuous to ask if I may—wait, no, I don't have to ask permission here.
I'm going, and I want you to come with me, {player}. You'll tell me if I look ridiculous in denim, right?

yelena.direction: Her room in halls, the trunk of gowns open and her sketches pinned over the crest. She wants to buy something ordinary at Bloom & Co. with her own money and nobody taking notes, and wants {player} to come; she asked his permission by habit and caught herself. The family phone buzzed face down and stayed that way.

yelena.invitation: Meet me in Riverside Park by the low wall, {player}. I have a free hour and I really don't want to spend it indoors.

lines: *She is sitting on the stone wall in her cream silk blouse and green velvet skirt, twirling a bare willow slip between her fingers in the late afternoon light.*
You're always so quiet when we walk out here, {player}. You never ask me to do the thing.
*She closes her hand around the twig, and when her fingers open a tiny white blossom has forced its way through the bark.*
At Assembly dinners I'm basically a centerpiece between the soup and the fish, so I only do it now when nobody asks.
*She sets the flowering twig on the stone beside your hand and smooths her skirt.*
My father had me briefed on Queen Seraphine's shyness before I was twelve, and nobody at home pretends it's an accident I was enrolled in her year.
I am supposed to be the composed one, the brilliant alternative, like I'm a draft bill in committee instead of a girl.
What do you think happens if I decide I'm tired of being my family's good idea, {player}?

yelena.direction: Riverside Park, late afternoon: she brought a cutting to flower for him because he did not ask. Her father briefed her on the Queen before she was twelve and nobody at home thinks it an accident she is in the Queen's year; she has said what it is to be her family's good idea, and asked what happens if she tires of it.

yelena.invitation: Come to my room tonight, {player}. There is something I have already done, and I want to tell you to your face.

lines: *The Goldvine crest on her wall is bare tonight, the sketches taken down, and a sealed courier receipt lies beside her face-down family phone.*
In my house a woman chooses her Sire in the open, on her own terms, and the whole city is supposed to watch her choose brilliantly.
*She stands by the student bed in her ivory and green aristocratic gown, her chin up in the posture she uses for the Assembly galleries.*
I wrote to my father an hour ago and named you, {player}, and the messenger has already left the gates.
I also stopped taking my dampers at the start of the week, because I have no intention of doing this halfway.
I have never had a lover—not out of modesty, obviously, I just wasn't going to give the gallery a show until it was actually mine.
*Her shoulders drop an inch, the court polish cracking into a small, real smile.*
You aren't a move against the crown, {player}, and you aren't my father's strategy. I chose you, in the open—so what do you say to me now?

yelena.direction: Her room, the crest bare, a courier receipt beside the face-down phone. A Goldvine chooses her Sire in the open: she has written to her father naming him, and stopped her suppressant. She is a virgin and has said so without fuss. He is not a move against the crown or her father's strategy; she chose, in the open, and has asked what he says now.

lines: *The Goldvine crest on her wall is bare tonight, the sketches taken down, and a sealed courier receipt lies beside her face-down family phone.*
In my house a woman chooses her Sire in the open, on her own terms, and sneaking you up the back stairs was the only un-Goldvine thing I've ever done.
*She stands by the student bed in her ivory and green aristocratic gown, her chin up in the posture she uses for the Assembly galleries.*
I liked keeping you to myself, {player}, like you were the one thing in my life nobody had a briefing on, but I'm done hiding.
I sent a courier to my father an hour ago, and I told him I have already taken you to my bed and I've stopped my dampers.
It was three lines long, and I didn't ask his leave, because he is the one who taught me a Goldvine doesn't ask.
*Her shoulders drop an inch, the court polish cracking into a small, real smile.*
By morning the whole family will know you're mine, {player}. Come here and tell me you're glad I finally said it out loud.

ifIntimate.direction: Her room, the crest bare. They have been together in secret, the one un-Goldvine thing she has done; she has sent her father three lines saying she has taken him to her bed and stopped her suppressant, and did not ask leave. By morning the family will know. She wants to hear he is glad she said it aloud.

lines: *On the wall of her room in halls, the Goldvine crest hangs bare, and a stamped courier receipt sits beside her face-down family phone.*
A daughter of House Goldvine is expected to conduct her attachments in the light of day—which is, like, super intense when you actually do it.
*She taps the paper receipt with one manicured nail, catching herself before she can fold her hands the way she was taught.*
May I show you this—actually, wait, it's my room, I don't have to ask.
I sent a rider to my father an hour ago naming you, {player}, three lines total, and I didn't ask his leave.
You aren't a move against the crown or a piece in my father's strategy; I just wanted you, and I knew it the first morning you stayed and didn't care who my family was.
*She steps closer to you, her chin high even though her breath catches slightly.*
So it's completely out in the open now—what are you going to say back to me?

ifUnprotected.direction: Her room, the crest bare, the receipt on the desk. She sent a rider to her father naming him, three lines, no leave asked; he is not a move against the crown or a piece of strategy, she wanted him and knew it the first morning he stayed. It is in the open now and she has asked what he says back. Nothing about what her body is doing.

yulia.invitation: Rent week, babe, which means I'm pouring overpriced glow-rot at the Undergrowth. Come keep me company before my ears bleed. First one's free if you pretend to tip.

lines: *The Undergrowth is packed wall to wall, bass rattling the glass shelves behind the bar where Yulia catches your eye and grins.*
*She slides a neon-blue shot across the sticky wood, leaning on her elbows so you can hear her over the thrum.*
Look at you, {player}, walking in here like you've got an actual bedtime. That's so Breedhaven, honestly.
*The track cuts out between sets, leaving a sudden, ringing pocket of quiet under the crowd's murmur, and she twirls a bottle cap between her fingers.*
Everyone's my best friend when the bass is up, right? Got a hundred people in this room who'd buy me a bump and zero who know my mother's first name.
*She laughs, sharp and bright, then clicks her tongue at herself and shakes her head.*
Listen to me getting weird when I'm on the clock. Tell me something good, babe, before the DJ figures out the crossfader.

yulia.direction: The Undergrowth on her bar shift, rent week, the club loud. In a lull she said the real thing as a joke: a hundred friends in the room and nobody who knows her mother's name, and clicked her tongue at herself. "Babe"; "that's so Breedhaven"; she wants to hear something good before the music comes back.

yulia.invitation: Come up to my place above Byte & Bloom. Street's loud and I don't feel like going out. Door's unlocked, just kick the coats out of the way.

lines: *Streetlight spills through the open window of Yulia's studio, catching the strings of colored glass charms tangled above her unmade bed.*
*She stands near the speaker stack, pointing a thumb at a stiff square of waxed parchment pinned crookedly to the plaster.*
That's the Kaldra basin. My mom drew the storm-lines by hand while her eyelashes were literally freezing together, and I use it to cover a hole in the drywall.
*When you step closer and trace the steady northern runes with genuine respect, the easy grin drops off her face and she goes completely still.*
Yeah, well, like, don't go getting all academic on me, babe, it's just old ink and bad weather, my sister's got ten of 'em—
*She catches herself, lets out a breath, and leans her shoulder against the wall beside the map.*
Nobody here ever asks about home unless they want a story about snow. What made you look at it like that, {player}?

yulia.direction: Her studio over Byte & Bloom, late: the storm-line map in her mother's hand pinned over a hole in the wall. He looked at it with respect and she went still, which she never does, talked fast to cover it, then stopped covering. She has asked what made him look at it like that.

yulia.invitation: Come over to Lantern Row. Just you, nobody else, and I didn't even turn the speakers on. Don't make me wait around, okay?

lines: *The studio is unusually quiet tonight, only the muffled hum of Lantern Row drifting through the open window.*
*Beside the cracked mirror, the usual clutter of glass vials and silver spoons is gone, the wooden drawer beneath it pushed firmly shut.*
Don't look at the dresser like that, babe, I didn't get raided. Just... put it away for tonight.
*She sits on the edge of the bed, pushing a pile of winter coats aside, her fingers drumming fast against her knee.*
Still on my dampers, obviously, before you get some big True Sire complex about it. That's not what this is.
*She looks up at you, eyes clear and wide without the usual chemical gloss, and laughs once without any humor in it.*
I haven't done a night completely dead sober since I left Hjalmark, and it's kinda freaking me out, {player}. Come sit down and tell me I'm not boring like this?

yulia.direction: Her studio, the tray of vials shut away, the speakers off. She has taken nothing tonight, the first sober night since Hjalmark, because she wanted to be all the way here; she is on her dampers and this is not about that. Present, sober, scared of it, and has asked to be told she is not boring like this.

lines: *The studio is unusually quiet tonight, only the muffled hum of Lantern Row drifting through the open window.*
*Beside the cracked mirror, the usual clutter of glass vials and silver spoons is gone, the wooden drawer beneath it pushed firmly shut.*
Yeah, you're looking at the dresser. Put it all away an hour ago and I've been pacing a trench in the rug ever since.
*She sits on the edge of the bed, pushing a pile of winter coats aside, her fingers drumming fast against her knee.*
Still on my dampers, babe, that's not the thing. It's just that every time you and I have tumbled into this bed, I've been flying on something.
*She looks up at you, eyes clear and wide without the usual chemical gloss, her voice dropping its careless speed.*
I honestly don't know who I am in bed when my head's this quiet, {player}. You wanna find out with me, or is that too weird?

ifIntimate.direction: Her studio, the drawer shut. Every time before she was flying on something; tonight she is not, and does not know who she is in bed with her head this quiet. Still on her dampers; that is not the thing. She has asked whether he wants to find out with her.

lines: *Up in her cluttered studio over Byte & Bloom, the speakers are switched off and the little drawer of vials is pushed firmly shut.*
Look at us sitting in the quiet like normal people, babe—that's so Breedhaven it almost hurts.
*She clicks her tongue softly, sitting on the edge of the mattress and lacing her fingers together to keep them still.*
No, don't let me joke it off—I haven't taken anything tonight, first dead-sober night in longer than I want to say out loud.
I wanted to be all the way here when you walked through that door, no buzz between your face and mine.
*When you reach out to touch her shoulder, she goes completely still under your hand, looking up at you with wide, clear eyes.*
I've got a hundred friends in this town, {player}, and you're the only one who knows my mother's name, and that scares me way more than anything in that drawer.
So don't just stand there being sweet to me—say something, okay?

ifUnprotected.direction: Her studio, the drawer shut, the speakers off. Sober for the first time in longer than she wants to say, to be all the way here; a hundred friends and he is the only one who knows her mother's name, which scares her more than anything in the drawer. She has asked him to say something. Nothing about what her body is doing.

zelie.invitation: The house is quiet, mon cher, and I have left my door open off the hearth room. Come sit a moment if you are not yet asleep.

lines: *Her room off the hearth room is neat as a pin, the narrow bed made with hospital corners and the door propped open behind you.*
*Eleven short ribbons of different colors are tied in a row along the wooden frame of her mirror, above a neat line of perfume bottles.*
You are looking at my mirror, {player}. Sit on the chair—not the bed, I have just turned the corners—and I will tell you.

The pale blue is Bastien, from my first post in Port-Lumière, off his christening sleeve. Then Colette and little Luc, the twins in my first Sire house here—cream satin, because their mother had no sense of laundry.
*She touches each knot in order without looking, her fingertips moving down the glass.*
Mireille, the green velvet from a Yule parcel. Then the four at Highgate House: Nora, Pippa, Tomas, and baby Wren, who chewed the end of hers, voilà, you can still see the fray.
And the last three are from the house on the hill before I came to you—Sébastien, Clara, and Odette, who gave me the yellow grosgrain out of her own braid the morning the carriage came for me.
*She lets her hand fall from the frame and looks at you in the glass, her mouth curved.*
Four houses in six years, mon cher, and not one soul has ever asked me what the ribbons were for, non?

zelie.direction: Her room at Haven House, the door open to the hearth room: the eleven ribbons on her mirror, each child named in order and what the ribbon was. Four houses in six years and nobody has asked what they were for. Poised, teasing, "mon cher"; the house is {player}'s and she is its keeper.

zelie.invitation: I have a basket of table linen still to press in the kitchen. Come keep me company, {player}, if you can manage not to wrinkle what I have folded.

lines: *The kitchen is warm with starch and steam; she stands at the long board, running the heavy iron down a damask napkin without looking up.*

In Port-Lumière, after I finished at Sainte-Odile, I had a post with the Vaneau shipping house. Before the year was out, Monsieur Vaneau left a letter on my dressing table that a gentleman does not write to his child's governess.
*She folds the napkin into clean quarters, tuts softly at a crease no one else could see, and presses it flat again.*
I did not answer it, bien sûr, and I gave no cause for it. His wife found it in his blotter the next week, and after she was finished with my name, not a merchant house in the League would have me.
So I came here, where the Office pays well enough that my mother's shop stays open and my sisters have their schooling.
*She sets the iron on its trivet at last and looks across the board at you, both hands flat on the hot linen.*
Clause four of Miss Fairweather's contract is very plain, mon cher: a nanny who takes up with the Sire of her house is dismissed without reference before her trunk is packed.
I have been very careful for six years, and I have been trying very hard to be careful with you, and I am doing it badly.
Tell me honestly, {player}—you are not going to make this any easier for me, non?

zelie.direction: The kitchen of Haven House late, the house asleep, the linen pressed as she talks. She has told him about Port-Lumière, the letter, the wife, the houses that closed; and the Office contract: a nanny who takes up with the Sire of her house is dismissed without reference. She has been careful for six years and is doing it badly with him. "Non?"

zelie.invitation: Come to my room when the house is still. Do not knock, chéri, just shut the door behind you.

lines: *The door clicks shut behind you; on the narrow sill, the brass listening-charm lies turned face down against the wood.*
*She sits at her dressing table before the eleven ribbons on the mirror, drawing a new length of uncut white silk between her fingers.*
Do not look at the sill, mon cher. There is no child in this house yet to listen for, and tonight the room is mine.
For six years I have set other women's tables, and mended their linen, and tied a ribbon to my glass when the Office moved me on to the next door.
*She folds the white ribbon once over her thumb, her voice quiet and even.*
I have never said it aloud, not even to my mother: I want a table that is mine to keep, and a child I do not have to pack my trunk and leave behind.
I did not take my damper this week, {player}, and when Una Fairweather asks for my ledger on Friday, I am going to look her in the eye and lie to her.
*She rises and comes to stand before you, holding out the twelfth ribbon between you.*
Alors, chéri, before you touch me—tell me you understand what I am asking for in your house, non?

zelie.direction: Her room, the listening-charm turned face down, a twelfth ribbon uncut in her hand. She wants a household of her own and a child she does not pack her trunk and leave: never said aloud until now. She has stopped the suppressant and will lie to Una Fairweather. She has asked him to say he understands what she asks of a house that is his.

lines: *She shuts the door behind you herself and reaches past the curtain to turn the brass listening-charm face down on the sill.*
There. Two months of slipping down your hall after midnight like a thief in my own house, and I am finished with being careful.
*On her dressing table, beside the eleven ribbons on the mirror frame, lies a twelfth—new white silk, uncut.*
*She picks it up and turns to you, drawing the ribbon slowly between her thumb and forefinger.*
For six years I have kept other people's houses and loved other people's children until the season ended and the carriage came.
I have never said it aloud, {player}: I want a household that is mine, and a child whose ribbon stays on the glass because I am not leaving.
I stopped my dampers at the beginning of the month, and when Miss Fairweather inspects the ledger on Friday, I will lie to her face without blinking.
*She steps in close, pressing the coil of white silk into your palm and closing your fingers over it.*
You have had me in secret, chéri—now tell me if you know what I am asking of a house that is yours, non?

ifIntimate.direction: Her room, the listening-charm turned face down for good, the twelfth ribbon pressed into his palm. Two months of slipping down his hall like a thief; she is finished with careful. She has stopped the suppressant and will lie to the Office on Friday. She has asked, chéri, if he knows what she is asking of a house that is his.

lines: *In her narrow room off the hearth room, the listening-charm on the sill is turned face down on the wood.*
*Eleven small ribbons hang along the frame of her mirror from the eleven little ones she has minded, and a twelfth ribbon, new and uncut, rests between her fingers.*
Close the door behind you, mon cher, the house is finally quiet.
*She tuts softly at her own hesitation, drawing the uncut ribbon slowly through her palm.*
Six years I have kept other people's houses in order, {player}, always the borrowed caretaker, always packing my trunk when the contract ends, non?
Voilà—I am done being sensible, and I will lie straight to the Office on my reports if that is what it takes to never pack that trunk again.
*She steps up to you and presses the uncut ribbon into your hand, closing your fingers over it.*
I do not want a post anymore, I want a home that is mine—so tell me, chéri, do you understand what I am asking of a house that is yours?

ifUnprotected.direction: Her room, the charm face down, the twelfth ribbon in his hand. Six years the borrowed caretaker; she is done being sensible and will lie to the Office rather than pack her trunk again: not a post but a home that is hers. She has asked, chéri, if he understands what she asks of a house that is his. Nothing about what her body is doing.
